summary: The suite is larger and better-asserted than feared - 479 tests, measured 4 failed/475 passed in 283.50s then 2 failed/477 passed in 266.76s, 0 skipped, 0 errors, 0 testing functions with no assertion, 0 mock-call assertions, 0 bare assert True, every skip carries a reason - but the trust other agents place in it is misplaced in four concrete ways. (1) Running the suite starts the production FastAPI lifespan, whose temp-file cleaner immediately deletes any top-level file older than 24h in ./uploads and ./exports, and server/tests/test_api.py writes 16-byte junk .webm files into the real uploads/ directory (10 observed, 02:11-02:32 today). (2) Tests make live HTTPS calls to api.telegram.org (18 per run) because the lifespan starts the Telegram poller and the test DB carries a stored bot token; the conftest OMNIROUTE_API_BASE pin is inert since server/llm.py hardcodes openrouter.ai, so isolation is accidental rather than enforced. (3) The money path is untested: credits.charge, charge_with_rollback, deduct_credits_atomic, safe_deduct_with_rollback, refund and apply_discount have zero test references and /api/stripe/webhook has zero; the one economy test asserts >= lower bounds. (4) The CONTEXT.md known-red list is stale: the named deterministic red actually passes, and two browser_action_hardening tests plus test_run_python_math_bash_executes_safe_math fail unreported. Headline fix: a conftest that blocks non-loopback sockets, redirects uploads/exports to a temp dir, and suppresses the lifespan background loops; plus a CI job that deploy.yml actually depends on.

findings.title: Running the suite deletes real files from uploads/ and exports/ and writes test junk into the production uploads directory
findings.symptom: Running `pytest server/tests/` boots the production lifespan. The temp-file cleanup loop runs its first pass before its first sleep and purges every top-level file older than 24h in ./uploads and ./exports. The same suite leaves 16-byte garbage .webm files in the production uploads directory (10 present now). Owner/user files can be destroyed by an unrelated test run.
findings.root_cause: server/tests/conftest.py:31 uses `with TestClient(app) as c` (session fixture, conftest.py:28-33), which runs FastAPI's lifespan. server/main.py:187-207 is the production lifespan; lines 201-204 create the background tasks including `_cleanup_temp_files_loop` (server/main.py:167-184). That loop iterates `[./uploads, ./exports, /tmp/helpotron_exports]` (line 173) and `os.remove`s any top-level file with mtime older than 86400s (lines 175-181). The sleep is at the BOTTOM of the loop (line 184), so the first deletion pass executes within the first event-loop iteration of the test session. CWD is the repo root, so `./uploads` is the production /home/roni/Roni_workspace/helpotron/uploads. Separately server/tests/test_api.py:355,366 POST a 16-byte `lecture.webm`; server/transcription.py:28 sets `UPLOAD_DIR = BASE_DIR / "uploads"` and save_upload (server/transcription.py:37-43) writes `uploads/<uuid>.webm` with no cleanup and no test-dir override.

findings.title: Tests make live HTTPS calls to api.telegram.org; the OMNIROUTE_API_BASE isolation pin is inert
findings.symptom: Every test session emits 18 outbound POST https://api.telegram.org/bot<fake>/getUpdates calls that return 401. The suite is not offline, so it flakes on DNS/network/Telegram outage, and nothing stops a future test from calling a live paid API. The conftest 'never reachable' pin suggests this is handled when it is not.
findings.root_cause: server/tests/conftest.py:7 sets `os.environ['OMNIROUTE_API_BASE'] = 'http://localhost:9'` with the comment 'never reachable in tests', but server/llm.py never reads that variable: it hardcodes the endpoint at server/llm.py:429 and server/llm.py:606 (`https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions`). The pin only reaches server/config.py:52 (`omniroute_api_base`), which the LLM client does not consult. The live Telegram traffic comes from the same lifespan: server/main.py:206-207 starts telegram_agent_loop() (server/telegram_agent_link.py:339), which long-polls every stored bot token; the persistent test DB still holds a `telegram_bot_token` service setting from a previous test_telegram_agent run. There is no socket guard in conftest.

findings.title: CI exists but tests gate nothing: deploy.yml ships to production on a push to main without depending on the test job
findings.symptom: A red suite does not stop a deployment. Pushing to main runs the tests and deploys to the production VPS independently, so the reds have no consequence.
findings.root_cause: .github/workflows/ci.yml (push/PR to main) runs `pytest server/tests -v`. .github/workflows/deploy.yml (push to main or workflow_dispatch) SSHs to the VPS, does `git reset --hard origin/main`, pip install, npm build and `systemctl restart helpotron-api.service helpotron-bot.service`. deploy.yml has no `needs:` on the test job and no test step, so a failing ci.yml does not block it. findings.title: The test database is a persistent repo-root file that is never reset - state leaks across runs and drives the live polling
findings.symptom: Results depend on history: the DB holds hundreds of accumulated users and a stored bot token, so later runs behave differently from a first run. A fixed public_id can collide with a previous run.
findings.root_cause: server/tests/conftest.py:6 pins `DATABASE_URL = "sqlite:///./test_helpotron.db"` - a relative path resolved against CWD (repo root), not tmp_path or :memory:. The client fixture calls init_db() (conftest.py:28-33), which only runs Base.metadata.create_all (server/database.py:634) - no drop, no truncate. server/tests/test_api.py:18 states the persistence in a comment. So every run appends to the same file, and the lifespan poller reads it. This is NOT the production DB: server/config.py:30 defaults to `sqlite:///{BASE_DIR}/data/db/helpotron.db` and the conftest override is applied before server imports, so the prod-DB blocker does not apply.

findings.title: The assertion audit is largely clean - weaknesses are 15 truthiness-only tests and two tests asserting a stub's return value
findings.symptom: The feared failure mode is not widespread: there are no empty tests. The residual weakness is concentrated and cheap to fix.

findings.title: The git origin remote embeds a GitHub personal access token in cleartext in .git/config
findings.symptom: Anyone able to read the working tree, any backup of it, or any command printing remotes obtains a live GitHub credential that pre-commit and CI gitleaks cannot see.
findings.root_cause: The origin URL is of the form https://<token>@github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git. .git/config is untracked, so neither the gitleaks pre-commit hook (.pre-commit-config.yaml:2-5) nor the gitleaks CI job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:25-30) inspects it.

.pre-commit-config.yaml:2-5 and .github/workflows/ci.yml:25-30 - gitleaks scans tracked/staged content, not .git/config
findings.impact: Credential compromise if the tree is cloned, backed up or shared. Rotate the PAT and rewrite the remote to a credential-helper URL. Out of my track; flagged because it is severe.

def test_assignment_golden_path(client, unique_user):
    # 1. fresh user with a known balance

    # 2. create an assignment

external_research.why: The official recipe for loading an unpacked MV3 extension: chromium.launchPersistentContext(userDataDir, {channel:'chromium', args:['--disable-extensions-except=<path>','--load-extension=<path>']}), then take context.serviceWorkers() or waitForEvent('serviceworker') and read the extension id from the worker URL (never hard-code it - it is path-hashed). Only Playwright's bundled Chromium honours these flags; Google Chrome and Edge refuse them, which matches extension/CWS_APPROVAL_REVIEW.md:148's note about branded Chrome. MV3 workers suspend after ~30s idle and Playwright's existing handle survives the restart; only an in-flight evaluate() throws 'Service worker restarted'.
